comments.author: Jiblet
comments.body_html:
Love this mod, though I always add:

const MEDICAL_SUPPLIES = “57864c8c245977548867e7f1”

To the generateColumn function and the filter within it, allowing it to hold medical supply items like blood sets, syringes etc.

Seems in keeping with the item and not too cheaty.

comments.author: DezmoRizer
comments.body_html:
Your suggestion sounds great !

Can you explain in detail where exactly I should paste this line at ? or how it’s supposed to look like with this line?

Thank you!

comments.author: Jiblet
comments.body_html:
Sure thing. Open Mod.ts (TS, not JS).

Scroll to the bottom and you should see a section that looks like:

generateColumn(container: DependencyContainer, itemId, name, cellH, cellV) { const hashUtil = container.resolve<HashUtil>(“HashUtil”); const MEDS = “543be5664bdc2dd4348b4569”; const INJECTOR_CASE = “619cbf7d23893217ec30b689”; Add this line beneath the “INJECTOR CASE” line:

const MEDICAL_SUPPLIES = “57864c8c245977548867e7f1” That sets up a constant called MEDICAL_SUPPLIES that we can call upon a bit further down. The random-looking string of numbers and letters is the unique ID for all medical supply items (blood sets etc) in the Tarkov database, so we only need to add a single item here and not all of them one by one.

Then in the return call a few lines further down, you’ll see another reference to INJECTOR_CASE in a line about “the Filter”:

“Filter”: [MEDS, INJECTOR_CASE], Simply add our MEDICAL SUPPLIES constant to that list, making the line:

“Filter”: [MEDS, INJECTOR_CASE, MEDICAL_SUPPLIES], OR you can do it in a single line, but it’s less readable later when you want to work out why it’s not working.

Skip the first change I described, and just change the Filter line in the return call to:

“Filter”: [MEDS, INJECTOR_CASE, “57864c8c245977548867e7f1”],
